q: Which section of RA 9266 covers enforcement of the Act?
n: Section 44 of RA 9266 covers enforcement of the Act. It directs the PRC and Board to enforce the law, with help from government agencies and the integrated professional organization. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 44.

q: Which section of RA 9266 defines its terms?
n: Section 3 of RA 9266 defines its terms. It defines key terms such as architect-of-record, consulting architect and the scope of practice. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3.

q: Which section covers the powers and functions of the Board?
n: Section 7 covers the powers and functions of the Board. These include conducting the licensure exam, issuing and revoking registrations, and adopting the Code of Ethical Conduct and SPP. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7.

q: Which section covers CPD?
n: Section 28 covers Continuing Professional Development. It requires architects to keep their professional competence through continuing education programs. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 28.

q: Which section is "Prohibition in the Practice of Architecture and Penal Clause"?
n: Section 29 is "Prohibition in the Practice of Architecture and Penal Clause". Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: Which section covers liability of representatives of non-registered persons?
n: Section 31 covers liability of representatives of non-registered persons. It holds persons who represent or front for unregistered practitioners liable under the Act. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 31.

q: Which UAP SPP document covers specialized allied services?
n: UAP SPP Document 203 covers specialized allied services. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 203.

q: Which provision lists architectural interiors among the LEA subjects?
n: Sec. 14(3) lists Urban Design and Architectural Interiors among the LEA subjects. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14.

q: Which provision lists architectural interiors in the scope of practice?
n: Sec. 3(4)(g) lists architectural interiors (with space planning) in the scope of practice. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4).

q: Which provision lists structural design among the LEA subjects?
n: Sec. 14(2) groups structural design with building materials, specifications and utilities among the LEA subjects. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 14.

q: Which is NOT part of RA 9266's definition of structural conceptualization?
n: Structural conceptualization covers type, disposition, arrangement and proportioning of structural elements. Strength (analysis and design) is the structural engineer's work. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (definitions).

q: In the same situation, after publication, another architect notices some of their own work was credited to the featured architect. The featured architect claims it was done to help the writer get more advertisers. Who is liable?
o: Noone, since the featured architect is willing to settle
Both the featured architect and the writer
The featured architect, for fraudulently claiming another's work
The publisher, for not verifying the claims
n: Claiming credit for another architect's work, for any reason including publicity, is unethical. The featured architect should correct the credit publicly. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to colleagues); RA 9266, Sec. 33.

q: Where should an architect file a complaint that another architect claimed his work?
n: A complaint that another architect claimed one's work is an ethics and practice violation, filed with the PRC Board of Architecture. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7 and 22; PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct.

q: What is the maximum prison term for an architect found guilty under RA 9266?
n: RA 9266's penal clause allows imprisonment of six months to six years, at most 6 years, with or without a fine. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29 (penal clause).

q: What is the minimum prison term under RA 9266's penal clause?
n: The minimum prison term under RA 9266's penal clause is six months. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29 (penal clause).

q: Which is NOT an architect's responsibility to the public?
o: Using every means, including paid ads, to promote himself
n: An architect should not use every means, including paid advertisements, to promote himself. Self-promotion beyond dignified announcement is unethical. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the public).

q: Which is NOT an architect's responsibility to the client?
o: Offering only services he's competent in
Explaining the scope of his services
n: An architect cannot guarantee every estimate and cost. He gives probable costs and advises honestly. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the client).

q: Which is NOT an architect's responsibility to the contractor?
o: Knowingly calling on the contractor to fix his own oversights at the contractor's cost
n: An architect must not knowingly make the contractor correct the architect's own oversights at the contractor's cost. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the contractor).

q: What is the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture resolution amending earlier resolutions regarding the Code of Ethical Conduct for Registered and Licensed Architects?
n: PRBOA Resolution No. 5, Series of 2018 amended earlier resolutions on the Code of Ethical Conduct for Registered and Licensed Architects. Source: PRC Board of Architecture resolutions.

q: The latest version of the Architect's Credo was endorsed by UAP through NBD Board Resolution No. ____ series of 2017-2018.
n: The latest Architect's Credo was endorsed by the UAP through NBD Board Resolution No. 99, Series of 2017–2018. Source: United Architects of the Philippines board resolutions.

q: The architect's credo clearly states that it is the architect's duty to protect our common environment and to preserve the___ for the sake of the present and future generations.
n: The Architect's Credo binds the architect to protect the common environment and preserve the architectural heritage for present and future generations. Source: The Architect's Credo (UAP/PRBOA).

q: When was the Code of Ethical Conduct for Registered and Licensed Architects as well as for holders of Temporary Special Permits promulgated?
n: The Code of Ethical Conduct for Registered and Licensed Architects and TSP holders was promulgated in 2006 under RA 9266. Source: PRBOA Resolution (2006), Code of Ethical Conduct.

q: Which should the architect NOT do in relation to the client?
o: Give an overview of the project
n: The architect must not guarantee the project cost. He can only give a probable estimate. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the client).

q: The New Methods of Compensation that form part of the Standards of Professional Practice were approved by the Professional Board of Architecture (PRBOA) and took effect in:
n: The 2016 Architect's Guidelines, including the new methods of compensation in the SPP, were approved by the PRBOA and took effect in 2016 (Official Gazette, Sept. 2016). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (Official Gazette Vol. 112 No. 38).

q: Which should an architect NOT do with manufacturers and suppliers?
o: Accept free professional services and advice
n: An architect should not accept free professional services and advice from manufacturers and suppliers, because they create obligations that compromise his independence. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to manufacturers and suppliers).

q: As author and signatory of the contract, the architect may be sued by the client for breach in a:
n: As signatory of the service contract, the architect can be sued for breach in a civil case for damages. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1170.

q: How much will an architect pay if he violates the Code of Ethical Conduct?
n: RA 9266 sets fines of ₱100,000 to ₱5,000,000 for violations, with or without imprisonment. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29 (penal clause).

q: Which is an architect's responsibility to the public?
o: Respect and conserve the community's values and heritage and improve the environment
n: An architect's duty to the public includes respecting and conserving the community's values and heritage and improving the environment. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the public).

q: Who may file a complaint for violating the Code of Ethical Conduct?
n: Any person may file a complaint with the PRC Board of Architecture for violation of the Code of Ethical Conduct. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22; PRC Rules on Administrative Investigation.

q: Aclient wants you to be his architect, but you found out that there is another architect involved. What would you do?
o: Ask the client how much the design fee of the other architect is and lower your design fee
Call the other architect and ask for courtesy
n: If another architect is already involved, ask that architect as a courtesy before accepting. Taking over a commission without notice is unethical. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to colleagues).

q: As a newly licensed architect, which is unethical?
o: Taking a project another architect is already commissioned for
n: Stealing a colleague's intellectual property, immoral acts and taking a project another architect already holds are all unethical. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct; RA 9266, Sec. 22.

q: In what event is the Architect's Credo not recited?
n: Under PRBOA Resolution No. 5, s. 2018, the Credo is recited at mass oath-takings, PRBOA events and IAPOA affairs, not at induction rites. Source: PRBOA Resolution No. 5, Series of 2018.

q: Since he is already paid by the client, what must the architect never accept from suppliers?
n: Because the client already pays him, the architect must never accept commissions from suppliers. They compromise his duty to the client. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to manufacturers and suppliers).

q: Anewspaper editor approaches an architect for an interview. Which among the following is not ethical?
o: Ask to be paid for the interview
n: In an interview, asking to be paid and endorsing a product are both unethical uses of the press for gain or advertising. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to the public).
